text:
Taylor M: Quick design sync: compact pool card updates — min/max steppers, surge capacity control, SLO slider positioning. Need final copy + accessibility notes before dev sprint.
Ira P: Nice. Two high-level asks: 1) make surge visually distinct from baseline, 2) avoid popovers overlapping the cost widget on narrow panes.
Devon R: For 1) can we use a dashed outline for surge inputs + a small label "surge (temporary)"? That helps communicate ephemerality without extra verbs.
Lina Q: Dashed outline could be subtle. Also propose a small info icon next to the surge label with text: "Surge capacity is billed while active; reclaimed when load subsides."
Taylor M: Agree. What about action pattern — inline expand vs modal? Inline is faster but needs clear keyboard access.
Ira P: Inline expand is preferred. Tab order should be: Pool selector -> Min -> Max -> Surge toggle -> when expanded, focus moves to surge input. Use aria-controls + aria-expanded.
Devon R: Copy suggestions: primary header: "Capacity settings". Min label: "Min GPUs". Max label: "Max GPUs". Surge CTA: "Add surge capacity". Surge pill: "+{n} surge (temp)".
Lina Q: Microcopy tweak: replace "surge" in helper text with "temporary surge" to avoid confusion in analytics dashboards.
QA Z: Accessibility checks: keyboard-only flows? screen reader announcing changes when surge expands/collapses? Also test with high contrast mode.
OpsBot: Deployment note: API expects fields: `min_capacity`, `max_capacity`, `surge_capacity`, `surge_duration_seconds`. Update swagger.
Taylor M: UX nit — SLO slider guardrail tooltip currently sits on top of the cost number at <= 600px. Proposal: move tooltip anchor below slider and add small chevron so it doesn't cover numbers.
Ira P: Also add a small inline "why this matters" link that opens a non-modal panel explaining how guardrail interacts with SLOs and budget.
Devon R: Cost preview placement: prefer a persistent small row: "Estimated cost / hr" below the controls, so tooltips don't need to float over it.
Lina Q: Visual badge idea: pool tags (e.g., preemptible, nvidia-a100) should be compact chips after pool name. For accessibility include title attributes and a hidden text node for screen readers: "Pool tag: preemptible".
QA Z: Contrast: chips need >= 4.5:1 text contrast if they convey key state (preemptible). If purely decorative, 3:1 may be ok but we should avoid that for status.
Taylor M: Final microcopy proposals (for dev handoff):
- Header: "Capacity settings"
- Min label (aria-label): "Minimum capacity (GPUs)"
- Max label (aria-label): "Maximum capacity (GPUs)"
- Surge CTA: "Add surge capacity" (button with aria-expanded)
- Surge pill: "+{n} surge (temporary)"
- SLO guardrail short copy: "SLO guardrail — caps autoscale to meet latency targets. Learn more"
- Cost preview label: "Estimated cost / hr"
Ira P: Dev checklist (as single-line strings for copy-paste): "aria-labels for all inputs", "aria-expanded & aria-controls on surge toggle", "visible focus outline for steppers and chips", "tooltip anchored below slider at small widths", "screen reader live-region for guardrail state changes"
Devon R: UI note: avoid exposing internal units like "quanta". Convert `surge_capacity` from quanta to GPUs in display.
OpsBot: Reminder: update docs: /docs/console/capacity-controls after UI changes.
Taylor M: Thanks team. I'll update the figma file and add a prototype for keyboard flow. Ping me if anything else pops up.
OpsBot: Accessibility checklist template: https://go/redwood/a11y-checklist (bot)
